ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A tesseract is a 4 dimensional example of cube. It can be drawn in 3 dimensions by drawing two cubes and connecting their vertices together as shown in the picture below:

<image_1>

Now for the 3D equivalent. The lines connecting the vertices are replaced with ideal springs of constant $k=10 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}$ (in blue in the figure). Now, suppose the setup is placed in zero-gravity and the outer cube is fixed in place with a sidelength of $b=2 \mathrm{~m}$. The geometric center of the inner cube is placed in the geometric center of the outer cube, and the inner cube has a side-length $a=1 \mathrm{~m}$ and mass $m=1.5 \mathrm{~kg}$. The inner cube is slightly displaced from equilibrium. Consider the period of oscillations

- $T_{1}$ : when the springs have a relaxed length of 0 ;
- $T_{2}$ : when the springs are initially relaxed before the inner cube is displaced.

What is $T_{1}+T_{2}$ ?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, a large black wireframe cube surrounds a smaller black wireframe cube; the corresponding vertices of the two cubes are connected by blue line segments, showing a total of eight connecting lines. This is consistent with the meaning of the problem: these blue connecting lines are replaced by eight identical springs in the three-dimensional equivalent model. Reasoning: Take the common geometric center of the two cubes as the origin. The outer cube has side length b=2 m, the inner cube has side length a=1 m, the mass of the inner cube is m=1.5 kg, and the stiffness coefficient of each spring is k=10 N/m. Use the sign triple s=(±1,±1,±1) to mark the eight corresponding vertices, then the outer vertex B_s=(b/2)s, and the inner vertex after a small displacement u is A_s=(a/2)s+u. Therefore the connecting vector of the corresponding spring is q_s=B_s-A_s=((b-a)/2)s-u. T1: The natural length of the spring is 0. The force of each spring on the inner cube is k q_s. Summing over the eight vertices, the terms containing s cancel due to symmetry, leaving only F=-8k u. Therefore the equivalent restoring force constant is 8k, and the angular frequency satisfies omega_1^2=8k/m, so T1=2π sqrt(m/(8k)). T2: The springs are initially relaxed, so the natural length is the initial connecting length L=sqrt(3)(b-a)/2. The initial unit direction n_s=s/sqrt(3). After linearization for a small displacement, each spring produces a first-order restoring force only for the displacement along its own direction: F_s≈-k(n_s·u)n_s. Summing gives F=-k(Σ n_s n_s^T)u. The eight space diagonal directions are symmetric, Σ n_s n_s^T=(8/3)I, so F=-(8k/3)u. Therefore omega_2^2=(8k/3)/m, T2=2π sqrt(3m/(8k)). Substituting k=10 N/m and m=1.5 kg: T1=2π sqrt(1.5/80)≈0.860 s; T2=2π sqrt(4.5/80)≈1.490 s. Hence T1+T2≈2.350 s.

raw_record.question_text:
A tesseract is a 4 dimensional example of cube. It can be drawn in 3 dimensions by drawing two cubes and connecting their vertices together, as shown in the figure.

Now for the 3D equivalent. The lines connecting the vertices are replaced with ideal springs of constant $k=10 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}$ (in blue in the figure). Suppose the setup is placed in zero-gravity and the outer cube is fixed in place with a side length of $b=2 \mathrm{~m}$. The geometric center of the inner cube is placed at the geometric center of the outer cube, and the inner cube has a side-length $a=1 \mathrm{~m}$ and mass $m=1.5 \mathrm{~kg}$. The inner cube is slightly displaced from equilibrium. Consider the period of oscillations

- $T_{1}$: when the springs have a relaxed length of 0;
- $T_{2}$: when the springs are initially relaxed before the inner cube is displaced.

What is $T_{1}+T_{2}$?

method.method_draft: First read the figure as a large fixed wireframe cube surrounding a smaller cube, with eight blue connectors joining each outer vertex to the corresponding inner vertex. Treat those blue connectors as the eight identical springs. From the text read k=10 N/m, b=2 m, a=1 m, m=1.5 kg, and the two rest-length cases. Put the common center at the origin, with outer vertices B_s=(b/2)s and inner vertices A_s=(a/2)s+u for sign triples s=(±1,±1,±1), where u is the small displacement of the rigid inner cube. The spring vector is q_s=B_s-A_s=((b-a)/2)s-u. For T1, rest length is zero, so each spring force is k q_s; summing over the eight vertices gives F=-8k u, hence omega_1^2=8k/m and T1=2πsqrt(m/(8k)). For T2, the rest length is the initial connector length L=sqrt(3)(b-a)/2, and the unit directions are n_s=s/sqrt(3). Linearizing Hooke’s law gives F_s≈-k(n_s·u)n_s, so F=-k(Σ n_s n_s^T)u=-(8k/3)u by the symmetry of the eight cube diagonals. Thus omega_2^2=(8k/3)/m and T2=2πsqrt(3m/(8k)). Insert the numerical values and add the two periods to get about 2.35 s.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是一个大的黑色线框立方体包围一个较小的黑色线框立方体；两个立方体的对应顶点之间用蓝色线段连接，共表现出八条连接线。这与题意一致：这些蓝色连接线在三维等效模型中被替换为八根相同弹簧。

推理：取两个立方体的公共几何中心为原点。外立方体边长 b=2 m，内立方体边长 a=1 m，内立方体质量 m=1.5 kg，每根弹簧劲度系数 k=10 N/m。用符号三元组 s=(±1,±1,±1) 标记八个对应顶点，则外顶点 B_s=(b/2)s，内顶点在小位移 u 后为 A_s=(a/2)s+u。因此对应弹簧的连接向量为 q_s=B_s-A_s=((b-a)/2)s-u。

T1：弹簧原长为 0。每根弹簧对内立方体的力为 k q_s。对八个顶点求和，含 s 的项因对称性相消，只剩 F=-8k u。因此等效回复力常数为 8k，角频率满足 omega_1^2=8k/m，所以 T1=2π sqrt(m/(8k))。

T2：弹簧初始时放松，所以原长为初始连接长度 L=sqrt(3)(b-a)/2。初始单位方向 n_s=s/sqrt(3)。小位移线性化后，每根弹簧只对沿自身方向的位移产生一阶回复力：F_s≈-k(n_s·u)n_s。求和得 F=-k(Σ n_s n_s^T)u。八条空间对角线方向对称，Σ n_s n_s^T=(8/3)I，所以 F=-(8k/3)u。因此 omega_2^2=(8k/3)/m，T2=2π sqrt(3m/(8k))。

代入 k=10 N/m、m=1.5 kg：T1=2π sqrt(1.5/80)≈0.860 s；T2=2π sqrt(4.5/80)≈1.490 s。故 T1+T2≈2.350 s。

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as a symmetric cube-inside-cube arrangement: the blue segments run from each corner of the inner cube to the matching corner of the fixed outer cube. Because the visual arrangement is cubically symmetric, a small translation in any direction has the same frequency, so choose a displacement x along one coordinate axis. From the text use k=10 N/m, m=1.5 kg, and the two rest-length assumptions. For zero relaxed length, write the spring energy as U=(1/2)kΣ|r_i-x e_x|^2. The cross terms cancel because the eight connector directions occur in opposite pairs, leaving the quadratic term U_quad=(1/2)(8k)x^2, so K1=8k. For initially relaxed springs, the rest length equals the initial blue-connector length, and each connector is along a body-diagonal direction with x-direction cosine ±1/sqrt(3). A small x-displacement changes the length of each spring by approximately ±x/sqrt(3), so U_quad=(1/2)k·8·(x^2/3)=(1/2)(8k/3)x^2, giving K2=8k/3. Then compute T1=2πsqrt(m/K1), T2=2πsqrt(m/K2), and T1+T2≈2.35 s.

For T1, the spring relaxed length is zero, so the spring energy is U = (1/2) k sum |r_i - x e_x|^2. The eight connector vectors occur in opposite pairs, so the linear cross terms cancel. The quadratic term is U_quad = (1/2)(8k)x^2, giving effective spring constant K1 = 8k = 80 N/m. Thus T1 = 2π sqrt(m/K1) = 2π sqrt(1.5/80) ≈ 0.860 s. For T2, the springs are initially relaxed, so the rest length equals the initial connector length. Each connector lies along a body-diagonal direction, so its x-direction cosine has magnitude 1/sqrt(3). A small x-displacement changes each spring length by approximately ±x/sqrt(3). Therefore U_quad = (1/2)k·8·(x^2/3) = (1/2)(8k/3)x^2, so K2 = 8k/3 = 80/3 N/m. Then T2 = 2π sqrt(m/K2) = 2π sqrt(1.5/(80/3)) ≈ 1.490 s. Hence T1 + T2 ≈ 0.860 + 1.490 = 2.35 s.

A tesseract is a 4 dimensional example of cube. It can be drawn in 3 dimensions by drawing two cubes and connecting their vertices together, as shown in the figure.

The inner cube is slightly displaced from equilibrium. Consider the period of oscillations

- $T_{1}$: when the springs have a relaxed length of 0;
- $T_{2}$: when the springs are initially relaxed before the inner cube is displaced.

What is $T_{1}+T_{2}$?

Image description: In the figure, a large black wireframe cube surrounds a smaller black wireframe cube; the corresponding vertices of the two cubes are connected by blue line segments, showing a total of eight connecting lines. This is consistent with the meaning of the problem: these blue connecting lines are replaced by eight identical springs in the three-dimensional equivalent model.

Reasoning: Take the common geometric center of the two cubes as the origin. The outer cube has side length b=2 m, the inner cube has side length a=1 m, the mass of the inner cube is m=1.5 kg, and the stiffness coefficient of each spring is k=10 N/m. Use the sign triple s=(±1,±1,±1) to mark the eight corresponding vertices, then the outer vertex B_s=(b/2)s, and the inner vertex after a small displacement u is A_s=(a/2)s+u. Therefore the connecting vector of the corresponding spring is q_s=B_s-A_s=((b-a)/2)s-u.

T1: The natural length of the spring is 0. The force of each spring on the inner cube is k q_s. Summing over the eight vertices, the terms containing s cancel due to symmetry, leaving only F=-8k u. Therefore the equivalent restoring force constant is 8k, and the angular frequency satisfies omega_1^2=8k/m, so T1=2π sqrt(m/(8k)).

T2: The springs are initially relaxed, so the natural length is the initial connecting length L=sqrt(3)(b-a)/2. The initial unit direction n_s=s/sqrt(3). After linearization for a small displacement, each spring produces a first-order restoring force only for the displacement along its own direction: F_s≈-k(n_s·u)n_s. Summing gives F=-k(Σ n_s n_s^T)u. The eight space diagonal directions are symmetric, Σ n_s n_s^T=(8/3)I, so F=-(8k/3)u. Therefore omega_2^2=(8k/3)/m, T2=2π sqrt(3m/(8k)).

Substituting k=10 N/m and m=1.5 kg: T1=2π sqrt(1.5/80)≈0.860 s; T2=2π sqrt(4.5/80)≈1.490 s. Hence T1+T2≈2.350 s.
